samples.instruction: Seat the socket securely onto the M6 external-hex screw head, then call turn_socket once to unscrew and extract it through the modeled M6x1 thread. At every observation, use wristview-derived vision_screw_xy_estimate_m and vision_xy_error_m only when vision_confidence is at least 0.7. Below 0.7, hold x/y fixed and do not treat a zero error as alignment. Align x/y while holding z; the controller blocks downward motion while confident estimated XY error exceeds 2 mm. In force-controlled spiral-search mode, reassess estimated x/y error at every observation: stop x/y corrections only while confident error is at most 2 mm; if it later exceeds 2 mm, resume x/y correction. While aligned, the controller enforces continued downward progress. move_to z is an absolute world coordinate and smaller z means downward. Descend toward the visible screw top: use the full 5 cm safety-limited target change while the visible gap is clearly larger than 5 cm; as the top gets near, continue down through the remaining visible clearance instead of hovering above it or commanding an upward retreat. After XY alignment, when the estimated Z gap to the calibrated nominal screw-top plane is at most 5 cm, the controller ramps to a 1 N compliant axial-force setpoint by 1 cm and maintains that setpoint after contact; measured force may fluctuate. Once compensated tool-axis force reaches 1 N, contact takes priority over policy motion regardless of residual XY alignment. The controller latches contact and suspends Cartesian motion. Call the spiral_search tool exactly once to start the bounded search; do not issue move_to after contact. The spiral_search call blocks until stable seating, force protection, or the configured step limit, without intermediate LLM calls. It resolves residual lateral and external-hex phase mismatch. Never command an upward/retracting move after contact. Each increment moves the tip a small amount in the plane while rotating the socket 60 degrees. Search stops on stable seating, its force guard, or the configured step limit. A useful visual cue is that, after the socket is properly seated over the external-hex screw head, the screw head will normally be occluded by the socket in agentview; treat this as supporting evidence, not proof by itself. Do not claim contact until supported by visual or force evidence. Success is completion of the 21 mm threaded screw-extraction operation after stable seating. Do not use move_to to rotate the socket.

Continue with safe, purposeful motions until the goal is achieved or the environment step limit ends the trial. Do not stop early. You have a budget of 50 LLM calls for the whole trial.

UR20 with a rigidly wrist-mounted screwdriver and labeled agentview and wristview cameras. Use move_to with absolute world-frame Cartesian x, y, z targets in meters; each target change is capped at 5 cm in Euclidean distance. This is a hard safety maximum, not a recommended step size: when the target is clearly distant and the path is visibly clear, use the full allowed displacement; reduce motion size only near contact, uncertainty, or an obstacle. First align x/y while holding the current z, using the full safe displacement when far from the target and unobstructed. In force-controlled spiral-search mode, reassess image-derived x/y error at every observation: lock x/y only while confident error is at most 2 mm, and resume x/y correction if it later exceeds 2 mm. The controller follows the rising screw while maintaining axial compliance and returns only after extraction or a force/step safety stop. socket_turn_state contains active, signed socket angle in radians, and completion flag.
